section_summary: This section documents the diplomatic coordination, policy disagreements, and practical implementation issues surrounding General Douglas MacArthur's directive requiring the Japanese Government and protecting powers (Switzerland and Sweden) to surrender Japanese diplomatic and consular archives and property abroad to the Four Allied Powers. American diplomatic posts worldwide—particularly in Latin America (including Argentina, Mexico, Colombia, Paraguay, Guatemala, Honduras, and Uruguay) and neutral Europe (Spain and Portugal)—report on local conditions, host government sensitivities regarding sovereign custody versus Allied access, and administrative matters such as legation leases, safe openings, and internee maintenance. The file also reflects British reluctance to pressure belligerent host governments that insist on taking custody themselves, French requests to participate as an Allied power, and inquiries into captured Japanese embassy financial archives in Berlin.

subfiles.about: Memorandum of conversation clarifying the United States policy against being satisfied with mere access to Japanese archives in Argentina and elsewhere.
subfiles.summary: Straus tells Ranken the U.S. seeks full turnover of Japanese archives to the Four Powers after MacArthur's directives, notably in Argentina where ambassadors planned a fait accompli with the Swiss Minister; Ranken will have London clarify instructions.
subfiles.title: Japanese Archives -- Confusion between U K and U S with regard to Department's policy

subfiles.about: British Embassy telegram reporting on State Department instructions regarding MacArthur's forthcoming directive on Japanese archives and property abroad.
subfiles.summary: British Embassy telegram to London: MacArthur reportedly objected to parts of the suggested procedure, and State hoped belligerents would surrender archives but might accept examination if host states insist on custody.
subfiles.title: Telegram from British Embassy, Washington, to Foreign Office, London, regarding Japanese Archives Directive

subfiles.about: Letter clarifying the legal distinction between sovereign host-nation action prior to MacArthur's orders and Allied rights after Japanese instructions are issued.
subfiles.summary: Clattenburg tells Ranken a host power might demand custody before MacArthur's orders, but once instructions reach the protecting power without ending representation its claim is weak; in Argentina the Allies should take archives from the Swiss promptly without inviting government intervention.
subfiles.title: Letter to G. R. Ranken regarding Policy on Japanese Diplomatic Property and Archives

subfiles.about: Instruction to the American Embassy in Quito regarding satisfaction with access to Japanese archives and the opening of a safe.
subfiles.summary: Byrnes tells Quito the Department is satisfied with access, since archives were turned over, and the Embassy may suggest authorities try to open the safe with the best help available.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 630 to American Embassy, Quito, regarding Japanese Archives and Safe

subfiles.about: Despatch reporting Allied consensus in Mexico City that the Mexican Government will insist on retaining custody of Japanese archives rather than surrendering them to the Four Powers.
subfiles.summary: Messersmith reports his British, Soviet and Chinese colleagues agree Mexico, a belligerent, will take sovereign custody and grant access, as with German archives, and urges authorizing that for Mexico and other American republics to avoid friction over archives unlikely to hold significant documents.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 26,916 from Mexico, D. F., regarding Japanese Diplomatic and Consular Archives

subfiles.about: Despatch pointing out the absence of Japanese archives in Guatemala and suggesting the withholding of relevant circular telegrams.
subfiles.summary: Woodward recalls no Japanese mission or archives ever existed in Guatemala and suggests the Department economize by withholding future circular telegrams on the subject.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 735 from Guatemala regarding Economy in Withholding Circular Telegrams

subfiles.about: Internal memorandum transmitting Ranken's letter of October 30 setting forth British policy on Japanese archives.
subfiles.summary: J. H. Hibbard forwards Ranken's October 30 letter to Philip Cherp, which asks whether Buenos Aires alone hasn't approached host governments under the August 14 circular.
subfiles.title: Office Memorandum regarding British Embassy Communication on Japanese Archives

subfiles.about: Diplomatic letter conveying British instructions that representatives should not press beyond access if a belligerent government objects to surrendering Japanese archives.
subfiles.summary: Ranken says Britain supports Four-Power turnover but finds remaining Japanese archives too unimportant to pressure objecting belligerents, so its representatives only request permission to examine them, a formal difference of view with the U.S.
subfiles.title: Letter from G. R. Ranken to Albert E. Clattenburg, Jr., regarding British Policy on Japanese Archives

subfiles.about: Telegram reporting British and American diplomatic concurrence in Brussels that Belgian custody with Allied access is preferable for Japanese archives.
subfiles.summary: Brussels telegram: the U.S. and British Embassies informally agree it's more convenient and secure for Sweden to hand Japanese archives to Belgian authorities with Allied access, and the Ambassador concurs.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1297 from Brussels regarding Japanese Archives in Belgium

subfiles.about: Memorandum recording the Department's position declining a French request to participate in taking over Japanese archives and property.
subfiles.summary: Cherp records advising Colquitt that France can't join the Japanese archives takeover because it would invite Dutch and other requests; Colquitt will draft a negative reply.
subfiles.title: Memorandum for the Files regarding French Request to Participate in Japanese Archives Takeover

subfiles.about: Request to the War Department regarding the processing and location of captured Japanese Embassy financial records from Berlin.
subfiles.summary: Frederick Lyon asks Military Intelligence for the whereabouts and processing status of two cases of Japanese financial records, to April 1945, captured in July 1945 at Berlin's Japanese Embassy, covering accounts in Germany, Spain, Portugal and the Balkans, routed via London.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Present Whereabouts and Processing of Japanese Financial Documents from Berlin

subfiles.about: War Department Military Intelligence Division routing slip circulating the State Department inquiry on captured Japanese financial documents.
subfiles.summary: Major MacBryde routes State's October 17 memorandum on captured Japanese Embassy financial documents to the Foreign Funds Section, with a certified copy describing the Berlin embassy and Yokohama Specie Bank ledgers.
subfiles.title: Military Intelligence Division Routing Slip with Copy of Memorandum on Japanese Documents
subfiles.to: Foreign Funds Section, Military Intelligence Division

subfiles.about: Telegram analyzing financial, custodial, and repatriation responsibilities regarding Japanese property and personnel in Spain.
subfiles.summary: Armour asks about assuming responsibility for Japanese archives, property and personnel in Spain, recommends leaving leased premises with the Swiss and not taking personnel until repatriation plans exist; Japanese officials submitted a 125,000-yen monthly budget and will need outside funding.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 2169 from Madrid regarding Japanese Archives, Property, and Personnel in Spain

subfiles.about: Circular telegram transmitting the text of General MacArthur's directive to the Japanese Government regarding diplomatic missions and archives abroad.
subfiles.summary: Byrnes sends the directive MacArthur will give Japan at noon October 25, 1945: protecting powers Sweden and Switzerland transfer Japanese archives to the Four Powers, hosts keep custody in specified Allied nations, neutral-country missions surrender directly, and personnel are recalled.
subfiles.title: Circular Telegram to All American Diplomatic Missions regarding MacArthur's Directive

subfiles.about: State Department internal memorandum requesting declassification of historical documents for inclusion in the Whiteman Digest of International Law.
subfiles.summary: David Peterson of the Legal Adviser's office asks Ely Maurer to declassify attached papers for the Whiteman Digest of International Law.
subfiles.title: Memorandum Requesting Declassification of Papers for Whiteman Digest of International Law

subfiles.about: Instruction to the Legation at Tangier to repeat its telegram concerning Japanese archives in Morocco to the Embassy in Madrid.
subfiles.summary: Byrnes tells the Tangier Legation to repeat its October 24 telegram 314 on Japanese archives to Madrid if not already done.
subfiles.title: Telegram to American Legation, Tangier, Requesting Repetition of Telegram to Madrid

subfiles.about: Letter protesting the Department's circular on Japanese archives and urging acceptance of Mexican sovereign custody with Allied access.
subfiles.summary: Messersmith criticizes the October 23 circular as ignoring field advice and risking friction, since Mexico and other Allied American republics won't allow foreign custody on their soil, though they'll grant access; he urges authorizing host custody with Four-Power access.
subfiles.title: Letter from George S. Messersmith to John Willard Carrigan with Enclosed Telegram Paraphrase

subfiles.about: Telegram reporting on the location of Japanese consular archives in Casablanca and military attaché records in Madrid.
subfiles.summary: Alling: French Morocco's only Japanese archives, from the former Casablanca Consulate, are held with furniture by the Spanish Consul; the Tangier attache's records went to Madrid in May 1944; none known in Tangier or Spanish Morocco.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 314 from Tangier regarding Japanese Archives in Morocco

subfiles.about: Despatch reporting the absence of Japanese archives in Paraguay and transmitting an explanatory memorandum from the Paraguayan Foreign Ministry.
subfiles.summary: Asuncion: the Spanish Chargé and Paraguay's Foreign Ministry confirm no Japanese archives exist; correspondence was burned before the 1942 departure, leaving a couple of flags; Under Secretary Campos's memorandum confirms Koseki left none.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1220 from Asunción regarding Japanese Archives in Paraguay

subfiles.about: Telegram warning that Tokyo press leaks announcing MacArthur's directive may provoke Argentine interference with the delivery of archives.
subfiles.summary: Cabot reports Buenos Aires papers printed United Press Tokyo dispatches announcing MacArthur's order, warning that if Argentina obstructs delivery, the premature publicity will be to blame.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 2659 from Buenos Aires regarding Press Announcement of Archives Directive

subfiles.about: Circular telegram transmitting the State Department's reply to MacArthur regarding local Four-Power coordination and access negotiations.
subfiles.summary: Byrnes sends State's reply to MacArthur: receiving archives and property is decided locally by consultation among principal Four-Power representatives without the U.S. acting for all, and access where hosts take custody is negotiated locally.
subfiles.title: Circular Telegram to Diplomatic Missions regarding Coordination and Access Procedures

subfiles.about: Telegram providing instructions on offering Argentina access to archives, Swiss routine functions, office leases, and expense sharing.
subfiles.summary: Byrnes authorizes Buenos Aires to offer Argentina access, if Britain concurs; the Swiss keep routine functions and internee support from Japanese funds, with payments reduced, office rental authorized if funds lack, shared storage costs, and property disposal held in abeyance.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1563 to Buenos Aires regarding Archives, Swiss Functions, and Leases

subfiles.about: Airgram confirming the absence of Japanese archives in Honduras and requesting exclusion from future circular telegrams.
subfiles.summary: Tegucigalpa airgram: no Japanese archives exist in Honduras, as the honorary consul's papers went to Washington in August 1945, and the Embassy asks that future circular telegrams not be sent.
subfiles.title: Airgram No. A-272 from Tegucigalpa regarding Japanese Archives in Honduras

subfiles.about: Telegram requesting authority to offer the Argentine Government access to Japanese archives when notifying them of the takeover.
subfiles.summary: Cabot asks authority to offer Argentina access in the note announcing Allied takeover of Japanese archives, as Braden agreed with British colleagues; the Swiss Legation will surrender the archives on Bern's instructions.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 2651 from Buenos Aires Requesting Authority to Offer Access to Argentina

subfiles.about: Telegram reporting Swiss readiness to surrender archives and detailing questions on internee allowances, office leases, and Japanese staff.
subfiles.summary: Cabot says the Swiss agreed informally to deliver Japanese property and archives immediately; he asks a definition of routine functions, notes 15,000 pesos monthly to interned diplomats, the terminated residence lease, a proposed downtown office, and Chancellor Tani's internment.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 2658 from Buenos Aires regarding Swiss Custody, Leases, and Internee Support

subfiles.about: Telegram informing the Embassy in Lisbon that implementation of MacArthur's directive by Tokyo has not yet been confirmed.
subfiles.summary: Byrnes tells Lisbon, referring to telegram 2165, that the Department hasn't yet learned whether Japan implemented MacArthur's directive.
subfiles.title: Telegram to American Embassy, Lisbon, regarding Implementation of MacArthur's Directive

subfiles.about: Telegram reporting consultations among Allied envoys in Bogota regarding Japanese archives, joint sealing, and legation lease expenses.
subfiles.summary: Wiley, with British and Soviet colleagues, dissuaded the Soviet Minister from turning archives over to Colombia's Foreign Office; they plan joint inspection and sealing under British custody, maintaining the legation lease with about 90,000 pesos of frozen Japanese funds pending instructions.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1321 from Bogota regarding Allied Consultations on Japanese Archives

subfiles.about: Telegram inquiring whether the Japanese Government has sent instructions to its Lisbon representative under MacArthur's directive.
subfiles.summary: Baruch reports an Embassy officer met British and Chinese colleagues on Japanese interests in Portugal and asks whether Japan transmitted instructions to its Lisbon representative under MacArthur's directive paragraphs 1-C and 1-D.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 2165 from Lisbon Inquiring on Japanese Government Compliance

subfiles.about: Memorandum of conversation discussing press announcements of MacArthur's directive with the Chilean Chargé d'Affaires.
subfiles.summary: Joseph Flack tells Chilean Chargé Bascuñán that Allied committees will receive Japanese archives and property from protecting powers, with routine protection under Switzerland or Sweden; with no Soviet representative in Santiago, the three present powers will consult, and archives will probably stay where they are.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation with Arturo Bascuñán regarding MacArthur's Directive

subfiles.about: Airgram reporting bank balances held in the name of the Japanese Legation in Montevideo.
subfiles.summary: Montevideo airgram: no Japanese archives in Uruguay, but the Japanese Legation's account at the Banco de la República holds 205,888.85 pesos; no immediate action needed pending instructions.
subfiles.title: Airgram from Montevideo regarding Japanese Legation Accounts in Uruguay
